Neuronal cell cultures exposed to a heavy metal and markers of neurodegeneration in vitro

Abstract
Differentiated neuronal cultures were treated for twenty four hours and the viability,
the oxidative stress markers and the processing of the amyloid precursor protein were
quantified.

Methods
Cells were maintained in a humidified incubator and differentiated with retinoic acid
before treatment. Each condition was run in six independent wells.

Results
Lead acetate reduced cell viability by thirty eight per cent after twenty four hours of
treatment. The reduction followed a monotonic trend across the four concentrations that
were assayed, and the same trend was observed in the two independent differentiation
batches. Reactive oxygen species accumulated in parallel, and the mitochondrial membrane
potential fell in the two highest conditions. Markers of Alzheimer pathology increased in
the treated wells and the increase was significantly larger than in the vehicle control.

References
1. Ibarra M. Neuronal differentiation protocols. J Cell Methods. 2016;22:14-29.
